dedupe_keys.name: vehicle crowd interaction pedestrian trajectories citr and dut datasets

description: Two sets of top-view pedestrian and vehicle trajectories that record how crowds move when a vehicle is among them, from the Control and Intelligent Transportation Research Lab at Ohio State University. The CITR dataset, about 340 pedestrian trajectories, comes from controlled experiments in a parking lot near the lab, with lab members walking in groups under front, back and lateral vehicle interactions. The DUT dataset, 1,793 pedestrian trajectories, was recorded at two crowded places on the Dalian University of Technology campus: an unsignalised pedestrian crosswalk and a large shared space where people and vehicles move freely. Both were filmed from a hovering drone with a down-facing camera, and trajectories were extracted from video and refined with Kalman filters; the last major update of both repositories was on 19 April 2019. Files: CSV per scenario for pedestrians and vehicles with position, velocity, heading, and a scale file converting pixels to metres. The paper appeared at the IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium 2019. Licence: not stated for the dataset in the pages read (the preprint carries the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence); free download from GitHub. Caveats: campus and parking-lot settings only, small crowds. Useful to calibrate agent-based pedestrian models of shared streets and squares; related records are not yet linked.
